system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for leo.martins using NTLM, from the same reported IP address, 203.0.113.250.
About 41 seconds after the second failure, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for leo.martins using Kerberos from that same reported IP address.

The reported source address and successful logon are concerning in light of the supplied context that there is no VPN and remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01; however, the records do not establish that this was remote administration or that the address identifies an unauthorized system.

The workstation records show UserAssist registry-value writes associated with paths that decode to Firefox and a Teams shortcut, but they do not link those events to the domain-controller authentication source.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available authentication evidence consists of only two failures and one success; it does not show what occurred before or after those events.
The records report 203.0.113.250 as the source, but do not identify the actual device or person behind that address or establish whether the address is an anonymized value.
The provided records do not include network, firewall, endpoint, or session activity that would corroborate the source or show what the successful logon accessed.
claims_not_established: Whether the successful logon was initiated by leo.martins, another authorized person, or an attacker.
Whether the reported source address corresponds to a real external connection or to an intermediary or anonymized value.
Whether the successful authentication led to access or actions beyond the authentication event.
Whether the failures and success were part of credential guessing or a legitimate authentication sequence.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate the reported source address and timestamps with firewall, network, and domain-controller connection logs; verify whether the address is anonymized.
Review subsequent authentication and resource-access events for leo.martins, including logon-session details and access to domain or file-server resources.
Check WS-LMARTINS-01 and WS-SOKAFOR-01 telemetry for activity corresponding to the authentication times, and confirm with leo.martins whether the activity was expected.
Determine whether any approved system or intermediary could have generated the reported source address and logon sequence.
